target.title: fix(file-transfer): reject oversized inline file writes before node dispatch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users sending inline `contentBase64` to the `file_write` gateway tool could exceed the advertised 16 MB decoded payload cap and still reach the node-dispatch path before rejection.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inline decode path now uses the existing plugin SDK base64 decoded-size estimator to reject payloads over `FILE_WRITE_HARD_MAX_BYTES` before allocating decoded bytes. This matches the existing media-source and node-host file-write size invariant without changing policy, configuration, provider behavior, or the paired-node command contract.

## User Impact

Oversized inline file writes now fail earlier with the same maximum-size boundary and no node dispatch. Valid inline writes, malformed-base64 rejection, and media-id based file copies keep the existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: oversized inline `contentBase64` payloads are rejected by the registered file-transfer plugin tool before gateway/node dispatch, while the same runtime path reaches the gateway transport for a valid small inline payload.
- Current-head runtime proof at `fa28f03a607bdcc4706bbbca831d60fab78033a8`: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` imported `extensions/file-transfer/index.ts`, registered the actual plugin tools and node-host commands, executed the registered lazy `file_write` tool with a loopback `ws://127.0.0.1:<redacted-port>` sentinel gateway, and produced this redacted transcript:

```json
{
  "head": "fa28f03a607bdcc4706bbbca831d60fab78033a8",
  "plugin": "file-transfer",
  "registeredNodeHostCommands": ["file.fetch", "dir.list", "dir.fetch", "file.write"],
  "registeredTools": ["file_fetch", "dir_list", "dir_fetch", "file_write"],
  "hardMaxBytes": 16777216,
  "cases": [
    {
      "kind": "oversized-inline",
      "estimatedDecodedBytes": 16777217,
      "invocation": {
        "ok": false,
        "name": "Error",
        "message": "decoded content is 16777217 bytes; maximum is 16777216 bytes (16.00 MB)"
      },
      "dispatchObservation": {
        "sentinelGatewayUrl": "ws://127.0.0.1:<redacted-port>",
        "tcpConnectionsToSentinelGateway": 0,
        "gatewayDispatchObserved": false
      }
    },
    {
      "kind": "valid-small-control",
      "estimatedDecodedBytes": 2,
      "dispatchObservation": {
        "sentinelGatewayUrl": "ws://127.0.0.1:<redacted-port>",
        "tcpConnectionsToSentinelGateway": 1,
        "gatewayDispatchObserved": true
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

- Focused regression at `fa28f03a607bdcc4706bbbca831d60fab78033a8`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/file-transfer/src/tools/file-write-tool.test.ts` passed with 1 file and 2 tests.
- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD --engine claude` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: the oversized inline runtime call returned the max-size error before any TCP connection to the configured gateway sentinel, while the valid-small control reached that same sentinel once. That proves the over-limit guard fires before `node.invoke` dispatch on the actual registered file-transfer tool path.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the file-transfer `file_write` gateway tool path, the media-source sibling cap, the node-host file-write cap, the plugin SDK base64 estimator contract, focused tests, and duplicate PR/issue searches.
